Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY dunning.mjs templates.mjs engine.mjs expiry.mjs holdout.mjs stripe.mjs admin.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# dunning-engine

After using this, you can now **win back failed Stripe subscription payments
with a plan per decline reason, on your own server and with your own
emails**, which used to mean paying a recovery service a cut of what it
recovers, or living with Stripe's one-size-fits-all retries.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/dunning-engine/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`** — pick a Stripe `decline_code`, see the exact schedule of
  emails and retries Dunning Engine would run, preview the email, and estimate
  what recovery is worth with your own numbers. Runs in the browser; nothing is
  uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`** — the recovery service. One Node process, **zero
  dependencies**, state in one JSON file. It receives Stripe webhooks, plans and
  runs recovery, and reports at `/v1/summary` and a read-only dashboard at `/admin` (enter your `ADMIN_KEY`; open cases, next steps, recovered counts).

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | Dunning Engine |
|---|---|---|
| Stripe Smart Retries + Stripe's failed-payment emails | Free, good, but one policy for everyone and little say over wording | Your schedule, your wording, class-specific plans |
| Churn Buster, Churnkey, Baremetrics Recover and similar | Paid, often a share of recovered revenue; your customer data goes to a third party | Runs in your account, no per-recovery fee, nobody else sees your customers |
| A script you write yourself | Easy to get wrong: duplicate charges, retrying lost cards, double emails | Idempotent, tested state machine; dry-run by default |

**It can measure whether it works.** Set `HOLDOUT_PCT=10` and a stable 10% of
customers (by hash of the customer id) are left alone: their failures are
recorded, but they get no emails, retries or cancellation. `/v1/summary` and
`/admin` then compare how often treated and held-out invoices end up paid, with
a 95% interval on the difference, and say when the gap is still within chance
and roughly how many invoices it would take to tell. Here the measurement is your own data on your own server, not a vendor's claim. The cost is real: held-out customers are not chased, so keep
the share small and the experiment short. If Smart Retries is still on in Stripe
it applies to both groups, so the comparison is "us on top of Stripe" against
"Stripe alone".

Honest limits: the dashboard at `/admin` is read-only, there is no in-app cancellation flow (see the sibling
`cancel-flow` venture) and no card-account-updater network access (the expiry
notice asks the customer instead). It does not claim a recovery uplift over
Stripe's own retries; measure that on your own data (`/v1/summary` reports what
it recovered). If Smart Retries already works for you, keep it.

## What it does

1. **Classifies each decline** (`dunning.mjs`):
   `hard` (lost/stolen/restricted card) and `update` (expired, wrong number)
   are **never retried**; the customer is asked for a different card.
   `funds` (insufficient funds) retries on a spread schedule that optionally
   nudges toward payday (1st, 2nd, 15th, 16th, Fridays; a heuristic, off with
   `paydayAware:false`). `soft` (generic/temporary) retries 1, 3, 6, 10 days
   out. `auth` (SCA) goes to the customer only.
2. **Emails with a link that never expires.** Customer-portal URLs are
   short-lived, so emails link to `/update/<signed token>` on your server, which
   mints a fresh Stripe billing-portal session on click. Wording is neutral:
   it never says "stolen" or "fraud".
3. **Re-plans when it learns more.** If a retry comes back `lost_card`, pending
   retries are dropped. If the customer adds a card (`payment_method.attached`)
   an immediate retry is queued. If the invoice is paid, voided, marked
   uncollectible, or the subscription is cancelled, the case closes and nothing
   more is sent.
4. **Does not double-charge.** Before every retry it re-reads the invoice and
   skips it unless it is still `open`; retries carry an idempotency key; webhook
   event ids are de-duplicated.
5. **Warns before the card fails.** Once a day it lists active subscriptions
   and emails each customer whose card expires within 30 days (or already has)
   once per card, with the same never-expiring update link, so many failures
   never happen. Customers already being recovered, and subscriptions set to
   cancel at period end, are skipped. Turn off with `EXPIRY_NOTICES=false`;
   change the window with `EXPIRY_DAYS`. Needs Subscriptions read on the key.
6. **At the end of the grace period** it alerts you (`ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`) and
   leaves the subscription alone, unless you set `CANCEL_ON_EXPIRE=true`.

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/dunning-engine
node --test        # 64 tests, no network
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=rk_test_... STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... \
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) LINK_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
PUBLIC_URL=https://dunning.example.com node server.mjs
```

It starts in **DRY_RUN** (the default): failures are recorded and every email or
retry it *would* do is logged, but Stripe and your customers are not touched.
Try it with a **test-mode** key and `stripe trigger invoice.payment_failed`,
read the log, then set `DRY_RUN=false` with `RESEND_API_KEY` and `MAIL_FROM`.

Setup in Stripe:

1. Create a restricted key: Invoices write, Customer portal write,
   PaymentIntents read, Customers read, Subscriptions read (expiry notices; write only if you enable
   `CANCEL_ON_EXPIRE`).
2. Add a webhook endpoint `https://<host>/webhook/stripe` for
   `invoice.payment_failed`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_succeeded`,
   `invoice.voided`, `invoice.marked_uncollectible`,
   `customer.subscription.deleted`, `payment_method.attached`.
3. Settings, Billing, Subscriptions and emails: **turn off Smart Retries / the
   automatic retry schedule** (and, if you want only these emails, Stripe's
   failed-payment emails), so exactly one system charges and writes to your
   customers. Enable the customer portal under Settings, Billing, Customer
   portal.

| Env | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | required |
| `ADMIN_KEY` | bearer token for `GET /v1/summary` and `/v1/cases` |
| `LINK_SECRET` | signs the `/update/` links |
| `PUBLIC_URL` | where this server is reachable (used in emails) |
| `RESEND_API_KEY`, `MAIL_FROM` | email sending (needed when `DRY_RUN=false`) |
| `COMPANY_NAME`, `COMPANY_ADDRESS` | email wording and footer |
| `POLICY_JSON` | override the schedule, e.g. `{"graceDays":10,"softRetryDays":[2,5]}` |
| `EXPIRY_NOTICES`, `EXPIRY_DAYS` | card-expiry heads-up emails (default on, 30 days) |
| `HOLDOUT_PCT` | share of customers left alone to measure uplift, 0 to 50 (default 0 = off) |
| `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` | Slack/Discord-style `{"text":...}` alerts |
| `STATE` | path of the JSON state file |

## One-click deploy (your own account)

Fork this repository and open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`.
`render.yaml` builds the `Dockerfile` here in **your** Render account with a
1 GB disk for the state file, and generates `ADMIN_KEY` and `LINK_SECRET`.
Nothing runs on the author's side. Fill in the Stripe and email variables in
Render's environment tab. State must survive restarts (open cases and
pending steps live in it), which is why this uses a paid instance with a disk
rather than the free tier. Docker anywhere works too:
`docker build -t dunning-engine . && docker run -p 8080:8080 -v dd:/data -e STATE=/data/state.json ... dunning-engine`.

## Status and what is not verified

Everything in `node --test` passes against a fake Stripe. It has **not** been
run against live Stripe by the author: do that in test mode before going live.
Email and consumer-protection rules for payment-failure notices differ by
country; you are the operator and responsible for them.

Files: `dunning.mjs` (classification, schedule; also runs in the browser),
`templates.mjs` (emails), `engine.mjs` (state machine), `holdout.mjs` (uplift experiment), `stripe.mjs` (webhook
verification, API calls), `server.mjs` (HTTP shell), `admin.mjs` (dashboard page), `index.html` (simulator).

Support the project: <https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood>.

## Other self-deploy paths

`docker-compose.yml` runs it on any box with Docker (the command is at its top). Fly.io: the steps are at the top of `fly.toml`. Both keep state on a volume and run in your own account.

VENTURE.yaml.text:
name: dunning-engine
description: >-
  Self-hosted Stripe failed-payment recovery: classifies each decline code,
  retries only where a retry can work (payday-aware for insufficient funds),
  emails customers a never-expiring update-card link, and closes the case the
  moment the invoice is paid. Browser simulator plus a zero-dependency server
  with a one-click Render deploy.
stage: prototype
owner: duncan

# Screened 2026-10-15. Paid market is real and proven: Churn Buster, Churnkey,
# Baremetrics Recover (formerly Recover), Stunning, ProfitWell Retain all sell
# involuntary-churn recovery to Stripe merchants, typically as a monthly fee or
# a share of recovered revenue. Stripe's own Smart Retries is the free baseline.
# The gap: merchants who want control of wording and schedule, will not hand
# customer data to a third party, or object to paying a percentage.
# duplicate_check: stripe-failed-payment-recovery-analyzer is a read-only CSV
# analysis of past failures; this is the live recovery service, a different job.
#
# First visitor: indie SaaS founders on Indie Hackers, r/SaaS, r/stripe and Hacker
# News asking "stripe failed payment recovery", "dunning emails self hosted",
# "churn buster alternative". Volume not measured with an external tool.
#
# Path to revenue (payments stay off): free and MIT as the lead magnet; a
# hosted version, done-for-you setup or GitHub Sponsors are the paid steps --
# hosting under the public name and billing are owner-gated.

hypotheses:
  - claim: >-
      Indie SaaS founders will deploy a dry-run recovery server on their own
      account once the simulator shows them a decline-specific plan, because
      Smart Retries gives them no say in timing or wording.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact
  - claim: >-
      Skipping retries on expired and lost cards, and linking a fresh portal
      session in the email, recovers more than a generic retry-and-remind
      sequence for the same merchant.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact

economics:
  currency: USD
  mrr: null
  monthly_cost: 0
  customers: null

budget:
  monthly_cap: 1
  protected: false

kill_criteria:
  - Fewer than three distinct GitHub users (issues, stars, or a pasted report) engage within 90 days of the page being reachable from the published site.
  - A user reports a double charge or a customer emailed after paying; the idempotency and close-on-paid paths come before any new feature.

links:
  production: https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/dunning-engine/
  analytics: null

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) LINK_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "dunning-engine-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"
  DRY_RUN = "true"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Stop losing subscribers to failed payments you could have recovered

Cards fail for very different reasons: an expired card needs the customer, an empty account needs time, a lost card needs a new card and a gentle tone. Treating them the same wastes retries and annoys customers. Pick a Stripe decline code to see the recovery plan Dunning Engine would run, then run the open-source server with your own Stripe key. No account with us, no per-recovery fee.

Preview a recovery plan

Class:

When (UTC)What happens

  


  

    
What is recovery worth to you?

    
Your numbers only: this page does not know your recovery rate and does not promise any uplift.

    

      

      

      

      

    

    
Extra revenue kept per month: - 

  


  

    
Run it yourself

    
git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/fp-monorepo && cd fp-monorepo/ventures/dunning-engine
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=rk_live_... STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_... \
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) LINK_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
PUBLIC_URL=https://dunning.example.com RESEND_API_KEY=re_... \
MAIL_FROM="Billing <billing@example.com>" COMPANY_NAME=Acme \
node server.mjs          # DRY_RUN=true until you set DRY_RUN=false

    
Point a Stripe webhook at /webhook/stripe for invoice.payment_failed, invoice.paid, invoice.voided, invoice.marked_uncollectible, customer.subscription.deleted and payment_method.attached. Turn off Stripe's automatic retries so only one system charges. Worried a deploy will drop a webhook? Put webhook-relay in front of it. One-click Render deploy and Docker are in the README.

  


  

    
Questions

    
Why not just use Stripe Smart Retries?

    
Smart Retries is good and free to try, and for many businesses it is enough. Dunning Engine is for teams that want the retry schedule and the email wording under their own control, want expired or lost cards to skip pointless retries entirely, or do not want a per-recovery fee from a third-party recovery service. You must turn Stripe's own automatic retries off so the two do not both charge the customer.

    
Which declines should never be retried?

    
Hard declines such as lost_card, stolen_card, pickup_card and restricted_card, and unusable cards such as expired_card or incorrect_number. Retrying them only adds failed attempts. The right move is to ask the customer for a different payment method.

    
Is it safe to try?

    
It starts in dry-run mode: it records failures and logs every email and retry it would perform, but contacts neither Stripe nor your customers until you set DRY_RUN=false. Try it with a Stripe test-mode key first.

    
Where can I see how much I already lose?

    
Export your failed payments and run them through the Stripe Failed Payment Recovery Analyzer. If your webhook endpoint rejects Stripe's signature, the Webhook Signature Debugger shows why.

    
Where does my Stripe key live?

    
In the environment of the server you deploy in your own account. The author runs nothing in between and never sees your key or your customers.

  


  

    
Starting a subscription from a free trial? Trial Converter emails trials with and without a card on file and can extend a card-less trial once, from the same Stripe account.

    
Selling services on a quote? Sign Keeper gets the quote signed first, so the invoice you chase later has an agreement behind it.

    
Customers who cancel on purpose instead? Cancel Flow asks why and offers a pause or discount that fits the reason. To see what both do to your numbers, MRR Pulse shows MRR, churn and net revenue retention from a read-only Stripe key. Selling software? License Keeper issues and revokes license keys from the same Stripe account.

    
No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. They charge your customers and email them on your behalf: you are the operator, responsible for your own Stripe account, your terms with customers and the email and consumer-protection rules where they live. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice. Everything on this page runs in your browser: nothing you enter is uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# It starts in DRY_RUN: set DRY_RUN=false only after you have watched the log.
services:
  - type: web
    name: dunning-engine
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/dunning-engine
    dockerfilePath: ventures/dunning-engine/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: DRY_RUN
        value: "true"
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: LINK_SECRET
        generateValue: true
      - key: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
        sync: false
      - key: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
        sync: false
      - key: PUBLIC_URL
        sync: false
      - key: RESEND_API_KEY
        sync: false
      - key: MAIL_FROM
        sync: false
      - key: COMPANY_NAME
        sync: false
      - key: COMPANY_ADDRESS
        sync: false
      - key: ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL
        sync: false
